tool.name: DANTE_LTR retrotransposon identification
tool.command:
echo \$PATH &&
## Memory budget, when Galaxy knows one. dante_ltr 0.6 sizes its worker pool ## against it; without it the tool reads the scheduler environment, then the ## cgroup limit, then MemAvailable, and MemAvailable describes the whole node ## rather than the job. GALAXY_MEMORY_MB is defined only by some runners and ## never by PBS or the local runner, so guard it like GALAXY_SLOTS. Whole GB, ## truncated; below 1 GB pass nothing and let the tool detect. DLTR_MEM_ARG='' && if [ "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then DLTR_MEM_GB=\$(( GALAXY_MEMORY_MB / 1024 )); if [ "\$DLTR_MEM_GB" -gt 0 ]; then DLTR_MEM_ARG="--max_memory \$DLTR_MEM_GB"; fi; fi &&
dante_ltr --gff3 '$dante' --reference_sequence '$reference' -M $max_missing --output output --cpu \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --mode '$mode' \$DLTR_MEM_ARG && mv output.gff3 $te_ltr_gff && mv output_statistics.csv $statistics && if [ -f output_summary.html ]; then cp output_summary.html $html_report; fi && mkdir -p ${html_report.extra_files_path} && if [ -d output_summary_plots ]; then cp -r output_summary_plots ${html_report.extra_files_path}/; fi

param.name: dante
param.label: GFF3 output from DANTE pipeline - full output

param.name: max_missing
param.label: Maximum number of missing protein domains to tolerate in full length retrotransposon

param.name: mode
param.label: Detection strategy
param.help: Lineage mode requires a full lineage-keyed domain complement, which depends on the genome being well covered by REXdb. Core mode instead seeds on the ordered RT/RH/INT core - the order of those three domains identifies the superfamily - and classifies afterwards, so it finds elements whose accessory domains are undetectable. Use core for species poorly represented in REXdb; lineage otherwise.
param.option: Core - ordered RT/RH/INT core, classified afterwards

data.name: te_ltr_gff
data.label: LTR retrotransposons annotation (GFF3) based on DANTE annotation $dante.hid and reference $reference.hid

data.name: statistics
data.label: LTR retrotransposons detection summary based on $dante.hid and reference $reference.hid

data.name: html_report
data.label: LTR retrotransposons detection on $dante.hid and $reference.hid report

tool.help:
This tool uses output from DANTE annotation pipeline to identify full length LTR transposable elements. Output is in the GFF3 format and include annotation of 5' and 3' Long Terminal Repeats, Target Site Duplication (TSD) and primer binding site (PBS).
All identified elements contains set of protein domains as defined in REXdb_. Based on the results of detection of structural features, elements falls into five categories:
- elements with domains, 5'LTR, 3'LTR, TSD and PBS - rank DLTP - elements with domains, 5'LTR, 3'LTR and PBS (TSD was not found) rank DLP - elements with domains, 5' LTR, 3'LTR, TSD (PBS was not found) - rank DTL - elements with protein domains, 5'LTR and 3'LTR (PBS and LDS were not found) - rank DL - elements as cluster of proteins domains with same classification, no LTRs - rank D
.. _REXdb: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13100-018-0144-1
**Detection strategy**
Two strategies are available, and which one suits a genome depends on how well that species is represented in REXdb.
- **Lineage** (default) requires a full lineage-keyed domain complement. It is the more specific of the two and gives lineage-level classification directly, but it can only find elements whose accessory domains were detected by DANTE. - **Core** seeds on the ordered RT/RH/INT core instead. The order of those three domains identifies the superfamily, and classification happens afterwards. On a genome poorly covered by REXdb the accessory domains are often undetectable, so lineage mode misses elements that core mode still recovers.
Principles of detection of LTR retrotransposons is describet in github_ repository of this tool.
.. _github: https://github.com/kavonrtep/dante_ltr
